what: NXP Semiconductors makes chips for cars, industrial equipment and secure identification. Its products run engine and battery management, in-car radar and networking, bank cards and passports.
customers: Carmakers and their suppliers above all, plus industrial manufacturers, mobile device makers and payment card issuers.
money: processors, radar, battery management and in-vehicle networking
microcontrollers and connectivity for factories and devices
secure elements for payments and network processors
moat: Chips designed into vehicle platforms that stay in production for seven to ten years, with qualification cycles that keep competitors out once a design is won.
risks: Car production volumes have been falling in Europe and North America
Revenue declined about 3% in the last financial year
Customers worked down inventory after the chip shortage, which cut orders
Tariffs and trade rules affect a business built on global supply chains
opportunities: Electric and software-defined vehicles need far more chip content per car
Radar and driver assistance are growing faster than the car market
Margins hold up well because designs are locked in for years
watch: Automotive revenue and the book-to-bill ratio, which show whether the inventory correction has ended.
